description.p: Voyager is a fast file manager for Linux, modelled on Caja (MATE). It uses your desktop’s GTK theme, icons and bookmarks, and feels at home on MATE, but works on any desktop.

ul.li: Icon, list, compact and columns views
Split view with two panes, each with its own tabs
Tabs like a browser: reopen closed tabs, drag them between windows
An info panel with a folder’s cover picture or a file’s preview
Rename many files at once: change case, insert, remove, replace, number
Undo and redo of file operations, and copies checked against their originals
Checksums (MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, CRC32 and more) in a file’s properties
Your own context menu entries and thumbnailers, and every keyboard shortcut changeable

description.p: Voyager’s code was written by an AI, Anthropic’s Claude, directed and tested by its maintainer.

description.p: The address bar takes commands as Windows Explorer's does: cmd opens a terminal in the folder, a program's name starts it there, a web address opens in the browser.
Own names for network places, the menu bar can be hidden, new screenshots in the light and dark look, and the icon caches are refreshed on installing.
The look and layout of Windows Explorer: an address bar and a command bar, a navigation pane with Quick access, This PC and Network, and a This PC page with the drives and how full they are.
Windows shares: \\server\share addresses, Map Network Drive, network places reconnected at start and names of your own for them.
Also a font setting, a search box in the preferences, and an option to open new windows at This PC.
The prebuilt program for other distributions now includes the German translation, which the one of 1.0.0 was missing.
